content.text:
Both features are in and all 127 tests pass.

**`edit <id> <text>`** (`index.js`, `lib/todos.js`)
- It replaces only the text, so the id, completed status and `createdAt` stay as they were.
- Words after the id are joined and trimmed, like `add`. It prints `Edited todo #<id>: <text>`.
- A missing id, missing text, empty or whitespace-only text, an invalid id and an id that doesn't exist each give an `Error: …` message on stderr and exit code 1.
- The arguments are checked before `todos.json` is read, so a bad `edit` never touches the file. This also holds when the file is corrupted or missing.

**`list --pending`**
- It shows only the todos that aren't completed, in the same format as `list`. Plain `list` still shows everything.
- Any other argument to `list` is an error. The message changed from "takes no arguments" to "only accepts --pending", and I updated the one test that checked the old wording.
- If every todo is completed, it prints `No pending todos.`, which is my own wording. If there are no todos at all, it prints the usual "No todos yet" hint.

The usage text now lists both commands.

I added tests for both features: CLI behaviour, the corrupted-file cases, the pure functions and the end-to-end run through `node index.js`. I haven't committed anything.
